item.title: Confessional 1.23.0
item.description:
• Search by meaning: Ask, chat and the meetings search also find what was meant, not just the words. Runs on your Mac.
  • Choose Claude's model and thinking level (Settings → AI Models).
  • Record on iPhone or Apple Watch: new Voice Memos become meetings (Settings → Watch Folders).
  • Share a meeting as a web page, and send summaries to Zapier, Make or n8n with a webhook.

item.title: Confessional 1.22.0
item.description:
• Suggest people: on a project's People tab, the AI reads the project's meetings and suggests who belongs there, and which unnamed speakers are who (one click names them).
  • Someone introduced and called by name who answers is now named, even if they also mention someone else with the same name.

item.title: Confessional 1.21.0
item.description:
• Your meetings in Obsidian: a note per meeting in your vault, with date, people, project and length as properties, the summary, decisions, action items as tasks, and the transcript folded away. Settings → Obsidian.
  • Tick an action item in Obsidian and it's ticked in Confessional too, and the other way round. What you write below the line in a note is kept.

item.title: Confessional 1.20.0
item.description:
• Projects have a People tab: their regulars, people who keep turning up, and unnamed voices that sound like a regular.
  • Merge two names for the same person and they're one person in every transcript, action item and voice memory (undoable). Rename someone once and it changes everywhere.
  • Better at naming a project's regulars and invitees; someone who says Benjamin isn't taken for Benjamin.

item.title: Confessional 1.19.0
item.description:
• Meetings in Spotlight: search a meeting's title, people, project or words from its summary and action items, and open it from there (Settings → Shortcuts & Spotlight).
  • Control Confessional from Shortcuts: start/stop recording, star, add a note, ask your meetings, and read back your last meeting's summary or open action items. Confessional's own Shortcuts actions and Siri phrases come in an update.

item.title: Confessional 1.18.1
item.description: • Tidier live captions: the latest few lines in one block, like TV captions, with the speaker's name only where it changes and no empty space.

item.title: Confessional 1.18.0
item.description:
• Live captions during calls: in the call bar, transcribed on this Mac about a second after someone stops talking, with Scroll back and Catch me up (the last few minutes summed up). Captions button in the call bar; default in Settings → Transcription. Never shown in screen sharing.
  • Voices remembered automatically when the name on someone's video tile matches the name they're called by in the conversation (and they answer to it). Undo the clean-up or rename them and it's taken back.

item.title: Confessional 1.17.0
item.description:
• Better at telling people apart: NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 now decides who is speaking. On recorded meetings (AMI), about 30% fewer speaker errors overall and half as many mix-ups between people; quick back-and-forth and similar-sounding voices stay apart. People already known by voice are still recognised. Downloads once (about 190 MB).
  • Someone who says only a little in a long meeting now gets their own label instead of being folded into someone else.

item.title: Confessional 1.16.1
item.description:
• Screenshots of shared screens: moving video tiles are ignored, so a screenshot is saved whenever the shared screen changes (before, a call with screen sharing could go many minutes without one).
  • Transcripts say how each person got their name: by voice, from the call screen, or from the conversation.
  • Speaker turns: a short interjection in the middle of someone else's sentence keeps its own speaker.

item.title: Confessional 1.16.0
item.description:
• New speech engine: NVIDIA Parakeet, run on your Mac. About 10% fewer word errors than Whisper on meetings, and an hour of audio in well under a minute. English and 24 other European languages; other languages still use Whisper.
  • Names and terms from your vocabulary list are spelled right more often, without replacing ordinary words.
  • Voice recognition keeps a wider spread of each person's voice (different mics and rooms), so people are recognised more reliably.
